label: Farming reaches Britain
note: Around 4000 BCE; the date is a rounded convention.

label: Long barrows and causewayed enclosures
note: West Kennet, Windmill Hill, Hambledon Hill and the first enclosure at Maiden Castle (about 5,500 years ago).

label: Stonehenge: first ditch and bank
note: About 3000 BCE.

label: Avebury henge begun
note: Built and altered from about 2850 to about 2200 BCE.

label: Deep flint mining begins at Grime's Graves
note: About 2600 to 2100 BCE.

label: Sarsens and bluestones raised at Stonehenge
note: About 2500 BCE.

label: Silbury Hill built; first metal and Beaker pottery
note: The mound was raised between about 2470 and 2350 BCE. Copper, gold and Beaker burials appear in Britain at about the same time.

label: Holme timber circle (Seahenge) built
note: Timbers felled in 2049 BCE by tree-ring dating.

label: Fields and farmsteads divide the land
note: From about 1500 BCE; the last digging at Stonehenge dates to 1800-1500 BCE.

label: Flag Fen causeway built
note: In stages between about 1365 and 967 BCE.

label: Iron working begins
note: A conventional date for the start of the Iron Age.

label: First hillfort at Danebury
note: About 550 BCE; hillfort building begins across southern Britain around 600 BCE.

label: Great developed hillforts
note: Maiden Castle is trebled in size about 400 BCE.

label: Cross-Channel trade through Hengistbury Head
note: Italian wine reaches Britain; most amphorae predate 50 BCE.

label: Julius Caesar's first expedition
note: A second and larger expedition followed in 54 BCE.

label: Calleva and Camulodunon founded
note: Coin-issuing kingdoms in the south-east; Calleva was established about 20-10 BCE.

label: Roman invasion under Claudius
note: The army is widely believed to have landed at Richborough.

label: Colonia founded at Colchester
note: The first Roman city in Britain.

label: Boudica's revolt
note: 60 or 61 CE: Colchester, London and Verulamium burned.

label: Britain divided into two provinces
note: Britannia Superior and Inferior; the date lies between about 197 and 213.

label: Emperor Septimius Severus dies at York
Carausius seizes Britain
note: A breakaway 'British empire' until 296; the Saxon Shore forts belong to these decades.

label: The 'barbarian conspiracy'
note: Concerted attacks by Picts, Scots and Saxons; order restored by Count Theodosius.

label: End of Roman rule
note: About 410; no single event is securely recorded.

label: Ship burial at Sutton Hoo
note: About 625, dated by its coins.

label: Death of Bede at Jarrow
note: His Ecclesiastical History, finished about 731, is the main source for the two centuries before.

label: Offa becomes king of Mercia
note: Reigned 757-796.

label: Vikings raid Lindisfarne
note: 8 June 793.

label: Battle of Ellendun
note: Wessex overtakes Mercia; Kent, Sussex and Essex pass to Egbert.

label: The Great Army lands in East Anglia
note: York falls in 866/7, East Anglia in 869, eastern Mercia in 877.

label: Battle of Edington
note: Alfred defeats Guthrum.

label: Alfred and Guthrum's treaty
note: Made between 886 and 890; Alfred also occupied London in 886.

label: Edward the Elder and Aethelflaed retake the southern Danelaw
note: East Anglia submits in 917-918; Mercia is annexed to Wessex in 918.

label: Aethelstan takes York: a kingdom of all the English
Battle of Brunanburh
note: Site unknown.

label: Eric Bloodaxe expelled from York
note: End of Scandinavian kingship in England.

label: Battle of Maldon
note: Renewed Viking attacks and the first payments of tribute.

label: Battle of Brentford; Cnut wins the kingdom
note: Edmund Ironside's victory at Brentford was followed by defeat at Assandun and his death; Cnut became king of all England.

label: Stamford Bridge and Hastings
note: 25 September and 14 October 1066: the Norman Conquest.

label: Harrying of the North
note: Winter of 1069-70.

label: Domesday survey
note: Ordered at Christmas 1085; more than 13,000 places, but not London, Winchester, Durham or Northumberland.

label: William II takes Carlisle
note: Cumbria is brought into the English kingdom.

label: Death of Henry I: the Anarchy
note: Civil war between Stephen and Matilda until 1153.

label: Murder of Thomas Becket at Canterbury
Magna Carta
note: Sealed at Runnymede, 15 June 1215.

label: Salisbury Cathedral founded
note: The see moves down from Old Sarum.

label: Battle of Evesham
note: Simon de Montfort, whose parliament that year included townsmen, is killed.

label: Statute of Rhuddlan
note: Follows Edward I's conquest of Wales in 1282-3.

label: Great Famine
note: Harvest failures of 1315-17.

label: Black Death
note: Arrived at Melcombe (Weymouth) in June 1348 and had crossed the country by the end of 1349; 40-60% mortality is widely accepted.

label: The 'Great Drowning of Men'
note: A January storm surge finishes Ravenser Odd and much of Dunwich; plague had returned in 1361-2.

label: First poll tax
note: The best medieval evidence for the relative size of English towns.

label: First Battle of St Albans
note: Opening of the Wars of the Roses.

label: Battle of Towton
note: 29 March 1461.

label: Battles of Barnet and Tewkesbury
note: 14 April and 4 May 1471: Edward IV recovers the throne.

label: Battle of Bosworth
note: 22 August 1485: Henry VII, the first Tudor king.

label: Dissolution of the monasteries begins; union with Wales
note: Lesser houses suppressed from 1536, the greater by surrender in 1537-40; the Pilgrimage of Grace rises against it. The Laws in Wales Acts (1535-42) end the marcher lordships.

label: James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England
